answer: Bonds are keyed to a hardware root and reset to zero on any proven link between two accounts, including shared funding or a common transaction graph. Every submission carries a fresh nonce, so an answer cannot be replayed under a second key. The part I doubt is enrollment: proving a link is cheap when the attacker is careless and expensive when they are not. A wander through the transaction graph finds the lazy farms, the prism of one root split across many keys is caught at the next nonce check, and a haven of genuinely separate hardware still costs real money per seat.
